title: Forks
blurb: A fork attacks two pieces at once, and your opponent can only save one. Learn to spot forks for you and against you, then meet their cousins: pins and skewers.

core.title: A fork attacks two things at once
body: A **fork** is one move that attacks two (or more) enemy pieces at once. Your opponent can only fix one problem per turn, so you win the other.
Knights are the great forkers, because their L-shaped jump is easy to miss. But any piece can fork.

board.caption: The knight on f6 attacks the king and the queen.

core.prompt: Fork the king and the queen with your knight.
core.hint: Find the square from which the knight attacks both the king and the queen.
core.explain: **Nf6+** attacks the king and the queen at once. The king must move, and then **Nxd7** wins the queen.

core.prompt: Both black knights are loose. Tap the square where your rook forks them.
core.explain: From **f5** the rook attacks both knights along the 5th rank, and neither knight can attack it back. One of them falls.

core.prompt: Fork the king and the rook with your bishop.
core.hint: Check the king along one diagonal while attacking the rook along another.
core.explain: **Be6+** checks the king and attacks the rook on c4. The king has to deal with the check, and then **Bxc4** wins the rook.

core.prompt: A pawn can fork too. Fork the two rooks.
core.hint: Which pawn move attacks both a5 and c5?
core.explain: **b4** attacks both rooks. Black can save one (and may grab a pawn on the way), but you win the other rook for a pawn.

core.prompt: Fork the king and the rook with your queen.
core.hint: The king and the rook are both on diagonals that meet on one square.
core.explain: **Qd5+** checks the king along the diagonal to g8 and attacks the rook along the diagonal to a8. The king must move, and then the queen takes the rook.

core.prompt: Your knight can fork in two different ways, but only one of them wins. Find it.
core.hint: One of the forks comes with check.
core.explain: **Ne7+** attacks the king and the queen, and the check means Black has no time to save her. **Nd4** also attacks the queen (and the bishop), but Black answers **Qc1+** and escapes with check.

core.prompt: Why is a fork with check so strong?
options: The king must move, so the other piece cannot be saved
A king in check cannot be attacked again
A check lets you move twice in a row
core.explain: A king in check **has** to be dealt with. That uses up the opponent's turn, and you take the second piece next move.

core.title: Watch for forks against you
body: Before every move, look at your opponent's knights too. Where could one jump to attack two of your pieces? That square is a **fork square**.
If you see one, guard the square, or move one of the two pieces first.

core.prompt: It is your move. Black's knight is about to fork two of your pieces. Tap the square it would jump to.
core.explain: The knight would jump to **f3**, giving check to the king on g1 and attacking the queen on d2. Move the queen, or make f3 unsafe for the knight, before it happens.

core.title: Fork puzzles
core.intro: Find the fork. Each one wins material by force.

puzzles.hint: You are Black. Jump to the square that checks the king and attacks the queen.
puzzles.explain: The knight on f3 attacks the king and the queen. After the king moves, the queen falls.

puzzles.hint: A pawn can attack two rooks at once.
puzzles.explain: The pawn on g3 attacks both rooks, and neither rook can take it. Black cannot save both.

puzzles.hint: Check the king and attack the rook at the same time.
puzzles.explain: The bishop checks the king and attacks the rook on b3, so the rook falls next.

core.title: Forks for Black
core.intro: The same ideas from Black's side. The board is flipped, so take your time.

puzzles.hint: Check the king along one diagonal and attack the rook along the other.
puzzles.explain: **Qd4+** attacks the king and the rook on a1. After the king moves, the queen takes the rook.

puzzles.hint: Both white knights stand on the 4th rank.
puzzles.explain: The rook attacks both knights along the 4th rank, and neither knight can attack it. One of them falls.

puzzles.hint: Check the king and attack the rook with one bishop move.
puzzles.explain: **Be3+** checks the king and attacks the rook on c5, so the rook falls next.

deeper.title: The pin
body: A **pin** attacks a piece that cannot move without exposing something more valuable behind it.
Here the knight on c6 is pinned to the king. If it moved, the bishop would be giving check, which is illegal. So the knight is frozen.

board.caption: The bishop, the knight and the king stand in one line.

deeper.explain: The knight on c6 is the only piece that would expose its king if it moved.

deeper.prompt: Pin the black knight to its king with your bishop.
deeper.hint: Which bishop move attacks the knight with the king right behind it?
deeper.explain: **Bb5** attacks the knight on c6, and the king on e8 is directly behind it. The knight cannot move.

deeper.prompt: The pinned knight cannot run away. Attack it with a pawn.
deeper.hint: A pawn attacks diagonally. Which pawn move hits the knight?
deeper.explain: **d5** attacks a knight that cannot move away. Black can only defend it, so you win a knight for a pawn.

deeper.title: The skewer
body: A **skewer** is a pin in reverse. You attack a **valuable** piece, it has to move, and the piece behind it is left to be captured.
Here the rook checks the king along the c-file. The king must step aside, and then the rook takes the rook behind it.

board.caption: The king is in front, the rook is behind it.

deeper.prompt: Skewer the king and the rook behind it.
deeper.hint: Check the king along the file that the other rook is on.
deeper.explain: **Rc1+** attacks the king, with the black rook right behind it on the same file. The king has to move, and then **Rxc8** takes the rook.

deeper.prompt: What is the bishop doing here?
deeper.explain: The bishop attacks the knight, and the queen is behind it. The knight is worth less than the queen, so it is a **pin**. (The knight may move, but then **Bxd8** wins the queen.)

deeper.prompt: And what is the rook doing here?
deeper.explain: The rook checks the king, and a less valuable piece, a rook, stands behind it. The king has to move, and the rook behind falls: a **skewer**.

deeper.prompt: One more. What is the knight doing?
deeper.explain: One piece attacks two enemy pieces at once: a **fork**. A pin and a skewer both need the pieces to stand in one line.

deeper.title: Pins and skewers
deeper.intro: Three skewers and a pinned piece to win. Look for pieces that stand in a line.

puzzles.hint: Check the king along the long diagonal. The queen is on the same line.
puzzles.explain: **Bf3+** checks the king, and the queen on a8 is behind it on the same diagonal. The king must move, and then the bishop takes the queen.

puzzles.hint: The rook checks along the 4th rank, with the other rook at the end of it.
puzzles.explain: **Ra4+** checks the king along the 4th rank. When the king steps away, your rook takes the rook on g4.

puzzles.hint: You are Black. Check the king along the file where the white rook stands.
puzzles.explain: **Rc8+** checks the king along the c-file, and the white rook is behind it. After the king moves, the rook takes the rook.

puzzles.hint: You are Black. The knight on c3 is pinned to its king. Attack it with a pawn.
puzzles.explain: The white knight is pinned by the bishop on b4. **d4** attacks it, and it cannot move away, so you win a knight for a pawn.
